owner.occupation: English teacher at an international school

world.bio: English teacher at an international school in Xiamen, originally from Leeds. Six years in China, enough Mandarin to order and complain, not enough to read a contract. Weekend five-a-side league, lousy at it. My dachshund Pickle is better known on campus than I am. He had spinal disc surgery in August and we have been in recovery mode ever since.
skills_assets: Cambridge CELTA, PGCE, taught Years 7 to 11 English literature
Spare room that has been converted into a padded recovery pen
Foam ramps and a harness for Pickle that I ordered and sewed straps on
A WeChat account where about 40 parents tag Pickle photos
An old Skoda-like second-hand Wuling Hongguang (don't ask)

projects.name: Pickle recovery plan
projects.text: Surgery on 14 August at a pet hospital on Xiamen island, IVDD in the lower back. Surgeon, Dr Chen, said crate rest for six weeks then rehab. He recommended hydrotherapy, an underwater treadmill twice a week, to rebuild back leg strength. Haven't found anything in Xiamen. A pet physio in Fuzhou has a pool; I got three price lists as PDF screenshots with packages and sessions and I can't tell what's included.

projects.name: Year 10 'An Inspector Calls' unit
projects.text: Six weeks of lessons, essay due mid-October. Kids are surprisingly engaged by the class-guilt theme. Planning a role-play trial of the Birling family.

projects.name: Dad's 70th birthday trip
projects.text: Back to Leeds for Christmas. Dad's birthday is 28 December. Sister has booked a restaurant. I need to sort out Pickle's care while away; can't take him on a plane in recovery.

notes.text: Pickle managed three wobbly steps on the tiles today without the harness. I may have cried a bit in the kitchen. Don't tell the Year 9s.

Five-a-side: lost 7-2. Our keeper is a 52-year-old Taiwanese uncle who is better than all of us. Knee a bit sore. Pub afterwards, ordered 'two beers' correctly in Mandarin, felt superior for a full hour.

Dr Chen follow-up. X-ray looks fine, spine stable. 'Water sport,' he said, in English, meaning hydrotherapy. Twice a week at least for 8 weeks. Fuzhou is 2.5 hours by high-speed train there and back. Not sustainable twice weekly with school, though maybe on Saturdays.

Colleague Li Na helped me read the Fuzhou price list. Three tiers with something about 'session cards', 'first-evaluation fee', 'boarding'. She didn't know the veterinary terms either. Need someone who is actually good at this stuff.
Learning to read menus: today I recognised 鸡, 牛, 面, and 'something with 蛋'. Ordered what turned out to be duck blood soup. Ate it. Honestly not bad.
Mum on the phone about Dad's 70th. She wants a surprise. Dad hates surprises. Told her to just tell him. She said 'you're as bad as your father'.
Parents' evening. Three different parents asked about Pickle, one asked about their child. Fair.
Golden Week plan: stay in Xiamen, walk Pickle (carried in a sling) around Zhongshan Road. Might look into whether any local vets have rehab, or if anyone knows someone.

messages.text: Li Na: 他们这个套餐是十次一个疗程，包含评估吧？ Me: Is that 'includes evaluation' or 'evaluation separate'? Li Na: Hmm, I think the evaluation is 200 separate. Me: And boarding is per day? Li Na: I really don't know, sorry Tom.

Becca: Dad's 70th, 28th Dec, I booked the Italian on Roundhay Road. Me: Good. I'll be there 23rd. Becca: And Pickle? Me: He can't fly. Becca: Hire a pet sitter? Me: In Xiamen it's tricky. Becca: Bring him in cargo? Me: Absolutely not.
Dave: Tom, you playing Saturday? Me: Yes but Pickle's therapy might clash. Dave: You and that dog. Me: He's 5 kilos of muscle. Dave: You're 80 kilos of regret.
Clinic: 下周二复查，带上之前的片子。 Me: Thank you. Clinic: 康复的事想好了吗？ Me: Looking into Fuzhou.

calendar.event: Possible day trip to Fuzhou to see rehab centre

relations.about: Chinese teacher at his school, helps with documents and WeChat, knows nothing about veterinary language.
Turning 70, retired bus driver, hates fuss.
Organises everything, thinks Tom's life in China is a long gap year.

constraints: Can't leave Xiamen on weekdays; weekend trips only
Budget for rehab roughly 6,000 RMB a month at most
Needs everything explained in English or very simple Chinese
Pickle can't be left alone more than four hours
sensitive: Surgery cost 22,000 RMB, partly on credit
Worried he'll lose the dog or that Pickle won't walk properly again
Loneliness: most of his friends are other teachers who rotate out every two years
